Metabolic pathways inferred from the Prokka annotations with MinPath. Commands for this step were run in `minpath/`.

# Step 8: Infer metabolic pathways

## Preparing the input for one bin

Moved into the `minpath` folder

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/minpath
```

MinPath input is prepared from each bin's Prokka `.tsv` file, so I looked at the file for a single bin first (`metabat.66`), then checked a second bin (`metabat.7`) to make sure the format was the same

```{bash}
head ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv
```

Just wanna try another one

```{bash}
head ../prokka/metabat.7/metabat.7.tsv
```

And it works

MinPath only needs a unique gene ID (column 1) and its EC number (column 5). Built the `awk` command up in steps, using `head` to test on the first lines:
  - `-F '\t'` tells awk the input is tab separated
  - `$5` keeps only the lines that have an EC number
  - `OFS="\t"` makes the output tab separated
  - `grep -v '^locus'` removes the header line

```{bash}
head ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv | awk -F '\t' '{print $1,$5}'
```

```{bash}
head ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{print $1,$5}'
```

```{bash}
head ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'
```

Swapped `head` for `cat` so all genes are included, and saved the output as `metabat.66.ec`

```{bash}
cat ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'
```

Create the .ec file

```{bash}
cat ../prokka/metabat.66/metabat.66.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.66.ec
```

run minpath on this file

```{bash}
minpath -ec metabat.66.ec -report metabat.66.ec.report -details metabat.66.ec.details
```

Ran MinPath on this file and looked at the top of the report

```{bash}
head metabat.66.ec.report 
```

## How to read a line of the MinPath report

- **PWY-7321**: the pathway ID in the MetaCyc database, which can be used to look up the full pathway ([PWY-7321](https://biocyc.org/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-7321))
- **naive 1**: at least one gene from the pathway was found. Calling a pathway present whenever one gene is found is the "naive" approach
- **minpath 1**: MinPath kept the pathway in its minimal set. `minpath 0` means the genes found are better explained by other pathways, so the evidence is weak
- **fam0 4**: four gene families are involved in the pathway
- **fam-found 2**: two of those gene families were found in this genome
- **name**: the pathway name (here, ecdysteroid metabolism in arthropods)

## Running MinPath on all bins
Prokka had finished, so I prepared the `.ec` input for every top bin and then ran MinPath on each one. This didn't take long

```{bash}
while read bin;do 
  cat ../prokka/$bin/${bin}.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{printf("%s\t%s\n", $1,$5)}' | grep -v '^locus' > ${bin}.ec 
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

```{bash}
while read bin;do 
  minpath -ec ${bin}.ec -report ${bin}.ec.report -details ${bin}.ec.details
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

There is far too much output to read it all, so I looked at two pathways only

## Pathway 1: photosynthesis light reactions (PWY-101)

This pathway includes the essential light-driven parts of photosynthesis, Photosystem I and Photosystem II

```{bash}
grep 'PWY-101' *.ec.report
```

This pathway includes the essential components of photosynthesis that occur in light, Photosystem I and Photosystem II.

- I got 4 lines, all for photosynthesis light reactions

**Question 4.1**

- **How many bins contain at least one gene from this pathway?** Four bins: `contig_126`, `metabat.66`, `metabat.7` and `metabat.9`
- **Which bin has all of the genes?** Only `metabat.66`, which has fam-found 4 out of fam0 4, so it has every gene family in the pathway
- **For which bins does MinPath keep the pathway (`minpath 1`)?** Two bins, `metabat.66` and `metabat.7`

Cross-referenced the four bins with the gtdbtk summary to see their taxonomy

```{bash}
grep 'contig_126' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
grep 'metabat.66' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
grep 'metabat.7' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
grep 'metabat.9' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

## Pathway 2: superpathway of tetrathionate reduction (PWY-5360)

This pathway includes enzymes needed to reduce sulfite to hydrogen sulfide, so it is a marker for sulfate reduction

```{bash}
grep 'PWY-5360' *.ec.report
grep 'metabat.30' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

**Question 4.2**

- **How many bins contain PWY-5360?** Only one, `metabat.30`
- **What order do these bins belong to? Are they in the same family?** The bin belongs to the order Campylobacterales. There is only one bin, so there is no comparison of families
- **How strong is the evidence?** Weak. MinPath did not keep the pathway (`minpath 0`) and only 1 of its 3 gene families (fam-found 1, fam0 3) was found in the bin
